text:
alex: Quick check — we're finalizing the async job contract for the new inference batch flow. Two quick things: (1) what should the initial response shape be (headers + body)? (2) cancel semantics + backward-compat expectations for older clients?

maria: Proposal: initial POST /jobs -> 202 Accepted + JSON body with job_id and status + Location header pointing to /jobs/{id}. Minimal example:

```json
{
  "job_id": "job_abc123",
  "status": "pending",
  "started_at": null
}
```

Also set `Location: /jobs/job_abc123` and include `X-Request-ID` echo if provided.

jyoti: For polling, do we return a `done` boolean like old api or the new `status` string? Need to know for mobile clients.

maria: Keep `status` as canonical. But add `done` as a compatibility field for one release cycle so old clients don't break. Map as: `done = status in ["succeeded", "failed", "cancelled"]`. After one major release we'll deprecate `done`.

sam: Implementation note: runtime can't immediately preempt in-GPU work. Cancel needs to be best-effort. Suggested cancel flow: POST /jobs/{id}/cancel -> 202 and set status -> `cancel_requested`. Worker observes request and transitions to `cancelled` or `failed` depending on whether it could stop cleanly.

alex: What about HTTP semantics for cancel? Should clients expect a final 200 on querying /jobs/{id} or a 410 sometimes?

maria: We should avoid 410. Always return 200 with job JSON. Final status field reflects lifecycle. Example final payload for cancelled: 

```json
{
  "job_id": "job_abc123",
  "status": "cancelled",
  "result_url": null,
  "error": null
}
```

jyoti: Timeouts — server-side TTL? Mobile wants predictable expiration so they can surface UI to users.

sam: Default TTL = 24h for queued/running jobs. After TTL expire we mark `status=expired` and `error` explains TTL hit. We can expose `expires_at` in the job object.

alex: Polling guidance for clients? backoff recommended?

maria: Yes: recommend client start at 200ms, exponential backoff to 5s; also support long-polling with `Prefer: wait=30` header. If `Prefer` provided, server will hold response up to that many seconds or until job completes. Avoid polling loops that hammer.

sam: Add note: when cancel is requested, `Prefer: wait` can be used on poll to observe quick transitions to `cancelled` without extra requests.

infra-bot: deploy pipeline: async-jobs-api v3 -> canary to staging in 10m :rocket: (automated note)

alex: Backcompat follow-up — we also had a boolean `success` key earlier for completed jobs. Will that be kept?

maria: We'll keep `success` for completed terminals for 2 releases but make it nullable. New clients should use `status` (succeeded/failed/cancelled/expired).

jyoti: Any special error codes for cancellation vs failure? i.e., client should retry on transient failure but not on cancelled.

maria: Yes: `error.code` values: `transient_compute_error`, `user_cancelled`, `expired`, `validation_error`. Retryable = only `transient_compute_error`. `user_cancelled` and `expired` are terminal.

sam: Also expose `attempts` and `worker_version` for debugging. Keep fields optional.

alex: Great — can someone drop a short RFC snippet we can link from the PR? I want to reference exact JSON shapes.

maria: I'll add a small spec doc and link in the PR shortly. Planning to keep the compatibility aliases for one major cycle and then remove them.

sam: Impl owners: @sam and @jyoti. I'll set a zap job to monitor canceled->final latencies.

alex: Thanks — this clears the questions I had. :thumbsup:
